q: How do I start?
a: Message Stevie on WhatsApp for a free consult, or book a free consult. No forms, no card, no contract.

q: Do I need to be fit already?
a: No. Every class is scaled to the person doing it. If you want to build up first, start with a Personal Training slot.

q: Can I try before I pay?
a: The free consult comes first, always, and if a class is the right way to start I will book you into one before you pay for anything. No card, no contract.

q: When does the next 8-Week Package start?
a: Monday the 28th of September 2026. Classes are capped at 25 people, so message early.

q: How much is the 8-Week Package?
a: £205, one payment. Every class on the timetable, small-group Personal Training slots, a nutrition plan, and measurements in week 1 and week 8.

q: How much is one-to-one PT?
a: £295 for ten private sessions, two a week over five weeks, nutrition included. Kids welcome at your session.

q: Is there a contract or a joining fee?
a: No. One payment, a start and a finish. You decide what comes next.

q: Can I pay in instalments?
a: Ask me at the consult. Deposits and split payments are sorted person to person.

q: Do you do gift vouchers?
a: Yes. Message me and I will sort a voucher for the 8-Week Package or one-to-one sessions.

q: What happens if Stevie is ill?
a: The terms cover it and they are worth reading before you pay for eight weeks up front. If a class or session is cancelled by Stevie for any reason, illness included, it is moved, and a one-to-one session is rescheduled.

q: What classes are there?
a: HIIT, Barbell & Dumbbell, Functional Fitness and the Saturday Full Body Workout. Fifty minutes, technique coached in every session.

q: What time are classes?
a: 6am classes Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday; 5:40pm classes Monday to Wednesday; Saturday 9am Full Body Workout. Personal Training slots 6am to 10am Tuesday to Friday and 7am and 8am on Saturday, plus afternoons: 4pm Tuesd

q: How big are the classes?
a: Small enough that Stevie sees every session. That is why places are limited.

q: Do I need to book classes?
a: Yes, through the Bookfit app once you are a client. Stevie sets you up at the consult.

q: What if I miss a session?
a: Book another one. A missed session is a missed session, not a missed week.

q: Can I do classes and PT?
a: The 8-Week Package includes both.

q: Where are you?
a: Spectrum House, 1A North Avenue, Clydebank Business Park, G81 2DR. Beside Singer station, free parking outside.

q: Is it a normal gym?
a: No. It is a private coached gym. No membership, no wandering about wondering what to do. You come in for a session and Stevie runs it.

q: Is there parking?
a: Yes, free, right outside the building.

q: Are there changing rooms and showers?
a: Changing space and toilets, yes. Ask Stevie about showers when you book.

q: Is it step-free?
a: Ask me before your first visit and I will tell you exactly what the access is like for you.

q: What results can I expect?
a: It depends on what you do. Most 8-Week clients who train three times a week and follow the plan lose fat, get noticeably stronger and feel a lot better. Your week 1 and week 8 numbers tell the truth.

q: Do you do nutrition?
a: Yes. Every package includes a nutrition plan written for you, and the members area has the Sanctuary baseline guide and a calorie calculator.

q: Do I have to give up alcohol or takeaways?
a: Nothing is banned. The plan runs on a 90/10 rule: if 90% of your meals follow it, the other 10% is life. Alcohol works against you, so the guide gives you weekend rules rather than a ban.

q: I have an injury or a health condition. Can I still train?
a: Usually yes, with a programme built around it. Tell me at the consult, and check with your GP if you are unsure.

q: Are you insured and qualified?
a: Yes. Stevie has been coaching since 2010, is fully qualified and insured.

q: I am over 50. Is this for me?
a: Yes. A good share of the gym is over 40, and strength work matters more the older you get.

q: I am pregnant or just had a baby.
a: Talk to Stevie and your midwife or GP first. Postnatal training is done one-to-one with a programme that respects where you are.

q: Can I bring my kids?
a: To one-to-one Personal Training sessions, yes.

q: Do you do sports-specific training?
a: Yes, one-to-one. Football, running, boxing, golf: strength work built around your sport.

q: Do you do corporate sessions?
a: Yes, for Clydebank Business Park companies and anyone nearby. Message me with numbers and times.

q: Is Sanctuary Fitness a gym or a personal trainer?
a: Both, in the sense that matters: a private coached gym with racks, bars and floor space, where every session is coached by Stevie. It is not a 24-hour gym you wander round on your own.

q: How much does a personal trainer cost in Clydebank?
a: Here, one-to-one Personal Training is £295 for ten sessions over five weeks with nutrition included. The 8-Week Package with classes and PT slots is £205. There is no joining fee.

q: Are there fitness classes in Clydebank for beginners?
a: Yes. HIIT, Barbell and Dumbbell, Functional Fitness and the Saturday Full Body Workout are all-levels classes, scaled per person. The free consult comes first, and I book you into a class before you pay for anything.

q: Is there a 6am class in Clydebank?
a: Yes. Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday at 6:00am, coached, done by 7 so you are at work on time.

q: What is the best way to lose weight in 8 weeks?
a: Coached strength training two or three times a week, a protein-first nutrition plan with a calorie target you can keep, more steps than you do now, and a measurement at the start and the end. That is the 8-Week Package.

q: How many times a week should I train?
a: Three coached sessions a week gets most people the result they came for. Two is fine to start. Six is available if you want it.

q: How much protein should I eat to lose fat?
a: Roughly 1.6 to 2 grams per kilo of bodyweight a day for most people training hard. The free calculator on the site gives you a number in thirty seconds.

q: Can I do personal training with an injury?
a: Usually, yes, around it rather than through it. Tell me at the consult, bring the advice from your physio, and the session is written for what you can do today.

q: Is personal training worth it over 40?
a: It is where it pays off most. Muscle drops faster after 40 unless you lift, and coached lifting is the safest way to start. A good chunk of the gym is 40 to 60.

q: Do you do couples personal training?
a: Yes. Two people, one coach, one session, both measured. Message Stevie for the two-person price.

q: Can I train while on Mounjaro or Wegovy?
a: That is a question for your prescriber first. If they are happy, coached strength work and protein-first eating are exactly what protects your muscle while the weight comes off.

q: Do you offer menopause fitness classes?
a: Strength training and conditioning built around recovery, in mixed all-levels classes or one-to-one. The menopause page explains what changes and what helps.

q: Is there parking at the gym?
a: Free parking at Spectrum House, inside Clydebank Business Park.

q: How far is the gym from Singer station?
a: About five minutes on foot.

q: Do you take walk-ins?
a: Message first. Classes are small and coached, so Stevie needs to know you are coming. A WhatsApp an hour before is usually fine.

q: Can I bring my kids?
a: To one-to-one Personal Training sessions, yes. Not to classes.

q: Do you sell supplements or meal plans?
a: No supplements. The nutrition plan is included in every package, and the recipe bank and protein cheat sheet are free on the site.

q: What should I wear to my first session?
a: Trainers, something you can squat in, a water bottle. Nothing else needed.

q: Do you offer online or remote coaching?
a: Not as a product. Everything here is in the gym, coached in person. Members get the plan, the recipes and the tracker online between sessions.

q: How do I leave a Google review?
a: clydebankpt.com/review takes you straight to the form. Two minutes, and it helps the next nervous person more than anything.

q: How much is a personal trainer per hour in Clydebank?
a: I do not sell by the hour. One-to-one is £295 for ten sessions over five weeks, which works out at £29.50 a session with the programme, nutrition plan and measurements included. Every price is on one page.

q: Is there a monthly membership?
a: No. Everything is sold as a block: the 8-Week Package at £205 or ten one-to-one sessions at £295. You pay once, train the block, and decide at the end.

q: Do I have to sign a contract?
a: No contract, no direct debit, no notice period. The block ends and you choose whether to do another one. Most people do; nobody is tied in.

q: Can I pay in instalments?
a: Message me. I would rather sort a way for you to start than lose you over the way it is paid.

q: Is the free consult really free?
a: Yes. Twenty minutes in the gym or on the phone, no card details, nothing to sign. If it is not for you, you have lost twenty minutes.

q: Do you sell gift vouchers?
a: Yes, for either package. The gift voucher page explains how it works; you pay by bank transfer and I confirm by WhatsApp.

q: What does the £205 actually pay for?
a: Eight weeks of every class on the timetable, small-group Personal Training sessions, a nutrition plan written for you, and measurements in week one and week eight. The full breakdown is here.

q: What classes do you run?
a: HIIT, Barbell & Dumbbell, Functional Fitness and a Saturday Full Body Workout. All fifty minutes, all coached, all in the 8-Week Package. The classes page has what happens in each hour.

q: What time are the morning classes?
a: 6am classes Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday. Done by seven, so you are at work by eight.

q: What time are the evening classes?
a: 5:40pm classes Monday to Wednesday. Home by seven with the evening done.

q: How many people are in a class?
a: Classes are capped at 25. I coach the whole class rather than lead from the front, so everyone gets watched.

q: Do I need to book classes?
a: Yes, with me, so the numbers stay under the cap. A message the night before is enough.

q: Can I try one class before I commit?
a: The first step is the free consult, in the gym or on the phone. There is no free week at the moment; the package is the way in, and there is no contract if it turns out not to be for you.

q: Are the classes suitable for beginners?
a: Yes. Every movement has an easier version and I scale people on the day. Beginners train beside regulars at their own level. What the first class is like.

q: Is HIIT safe if I am unfit or heavy?
a: Yes, because every jump has a low-impact option and you pick the version. The clock is the same for everyone; the intensity is yours. Anything medical, ask your GP first and bring the answer.

q: What is the difference between the package and one-to-one?
a: The package is coached classes plus small-group Personal Training and nutrition, £205. One-to-one is just you and me, ten private sessions, £295. Which to do first is a guide of its own.

q: When are the one-to-one slots?
a: Personal Training runs mornings 6am to 10am and late afternoons 4pm to 6:50pm. Tell me your shifts or the school run and we find a slot that fits.

q: Can I bring my children to a session?
a: To one-to-one sessions, yes. They sit where you can see them, with a tablet or a book, and you get your hour. Not to classes. The kids-welcome page has the detail.

q: Do you train couples or friends together?
a: Yes, in the same block at their own levels. How that works.

q: Do you write a programme for me?
a: Yes. One-to-one clients get a programme written for their goal and progressed every week. Package clients get the class programme plus the small-group sessions built round what they need.

q: Do you do online coaching?
a: No. Everything here is in the gym, coached in person. The tools, recipes and tracker on the site are there for the days between sessions.

q: When does the next block start?
a: Monday the 28th of September 2026. Places go by class size. Message me START and I will hold one.

q: What happens at the first session?
a: You are weighed and measured privately, we go through the health questionnaire, your nutrition plan gets written and your first sessions get booked. Then you train. The first-visit page covers the door, the parking and w

q: What should I bring?
a: Trainers, comfortable clothes, water. No gloves, no belt, no special kit.

q: Where do I park?
a: Free parking at the door of Spectrum House, Clydebank Business Park. Singer station is a short walk if you are coming by train.

q: Is there somewhere to change and shower?
a: Changing space and toilets, yes. Ask me about showers when you book. Most people arrive ready and shower at home or at work.

q: I have not exercised in years. Where do I start?
a: At the free consult. Then the first week is measurements and the easy versions of everything. Nearly everyone in the gym started exactly there. The beginners page.

q: Am I too old for this?
a: No. Clients are in their twenties to their sixties and beyond. The over-60s page and the over-40s page are honest about how it is scaled.

q: Is a diet plan included?
a: A nutrition plan written for you is part of both packages. Calorie and protein targets you can hold, foods from the shops you already use, nothing to buy from me.

q: Do I need to buy supplements or shakes?
a: No. The supplements guide lists the four that are worth the money and none of them are sold here.

q: How much protein should I eat?
a: Protein at every meal is the simple rule; members get the portion table for their appetite. The calculator gives you a number, and the cheat sheet shows 30g in 25 foods.

q: Can I still drink?
a: Yes, but the guide is honest about it: alcohol works against everything in the plan. Fewer drinks, water between them, a number set before you go out. The alcohol calculator shows what a normal week costs in calories.

q: Do you have recipes?
a: Thirty high-protein recipes under £3 a portion, most under twenty minutes, on the recipes page, with a shopping list builder and a meal builder.

q: What should I eat before a 6am class?
a: Nothing, or next to nothing: water, coffee if you want it, half a banana if you get light-headed. The breakfast after is the meal that matters. Full guide.

q: How much weight will I lose in eight weeks?
a: I will not give you a number, because I would be guessing and you would hold me to it. You are measured at both ends and the tape tells the truth. What eight weeks really looks like.

q: Why do you measure with a tape rather than scales?
a: Scales move with water, salt, sleep and the time of the month. A tape around the waist does not. Most people lose inches before the scales move. The longer answer.

q: Are the before-and-after photos real?
a: Yes. I take them myself, week one and week eight, same spot and same light, and clients choose whether to share them. The results page explains how.

q: What happens after the eight weeks?
a: We sit down with both sets of numbers and you choose: another block, one-to-one, or a break with the plan to keep going yourself. The three options.

q: Will I get bulky lifting weights?
a: No. Getting bulky takes years of eating and training for it on purpose. Eight weeks of coached strength work makes you stronger, firmer and usually smaller.

q: Where exactly is Sanctuary Fitness?
a: Spectrum House, 1A North Avenue, Clydebank Business Park, G81 2DR. Directions and a map.

q: Is it a gym or a gym?
a: A private coaching gym. No membership floor, no queue for a rack, nobody training beside you who is not in your session.

q: What areas do you cover?
a: Clients come from Clydebank, Dalmuir, Drumchapel, Old Kilpatrick, Bearsden, Milngavie, Dumbarton, Knightswood, Yoker and the West End of Glasgow. There is a page for each area in the footer.

q: Is the gym accessible?
a: Message me with what you need, step-free access, a quieter session, a chair, a longer warm-up, and I will tell you exactly what the building and the session can offer. The accessibility page has more.

q: Can I visit before I decide?
a: Yes. The free consult can be in the gym, and the door stays open on the Saturday before each start: the open morning is Saturday the 26th of September, 10:15am to 11:30am. Nothing to sign, nothing to bring.

q: Did the gym have a different name before?
a: Yes. It became Sanctuary Fitness in summer 2026. The coaching did not change with the name, and neither did the coach. The short version of the story.

q: I have a bad back. Can I still train?
a: Almost always, with the movements changed. Kettlebell hinges before barbells, box squats before free squats, no rep that changes your face. How we train around a bad back. Pain down a leg or numbness: GP first.

q: I am on weight-loss injections. Is training different?
a: Strength training matters more, to keep the muscle while the weight goes, and the protein target matters more still. The page on it. Your prescriber knows you are training.

q: Can I train through the menopause?
a: Yes, and strength work is the most useful thing for the sleep, the mood and the bones. Coached quietly, scaled on the day, nothing announced. The menopause page.

q: Can I train after having a baby?
a: After your six-week check and with your GP or midwife happy, yes, starting gently. The postnatal page has the caveats and the starting point.

q: Do I need a doctor's note?
a: Everyone fills in the health questionnaire before the first session. If it flags something, I will ask you to check with your GP before we start. That is for your safety, not paperwork.
